definition.simple: The list of buy orders and sell orders waiting at each price, with how many shares are wanted at each.
definition.balanced: A deep order book has lots of shares waiting near the current price. A thin one has only a few. In a thin book, a large [[market-order|market order]] uses up the best price and then fills at worse and worse prices. The visible book can also change or vanish in an instant.

example: Fictional bids: 3,000 shares at 0.40, 2,000 at 0.38, 5,000 at 0.35. Selling 10,000 at market fills at all three levels, an average of 0.371.
